title: The first dinosaur gets a name
subject: Megalosaurus bucklandii
summary: William Buckland describes Megalosaurus from a jaw and bones from Stonesfield, England. It is the first non-avian dinosaur to receive a scientific name, though 'dinosaur' does not yet exist as a category.

title: Dinosauria is named
subject: Dinosauria
summary: Richard Owen groups Megalosaurus, Iguanodon and Hylaeosaurus into Dinosauria. His reconstruction presents them as large, quadrupedal reptiles; later work will overturn much of that posture and biology.

title: Allosaurus is described
subject: Allosaurus fragilis
summary: O. C. Marsh names Allosaurus from the Morrison Formation. The Cleveland-Lloyd quarry, worked from the 1920s, will make it one of the best-sampled Jurassic theropods.

title: Triceratops is described
subject: Triceratops horridus
summary: Marsh names Triceratops from a skull fragment collected near Denver two years earlier. Complete skulls later reveal the scale of its horns and frill.

title: Tyrannosaurus rex is named
subject: Tyrannosaurus rex
summary: Barnum Brown's 1902 collection from Montana becomes the basis for Osborn's Tyrannosaurus rex. Early mounts stand the animal upright with a dragging tail, a posture that will persist for decades.

title: Spinosaurus enters the record
subject: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
summary: Ernst Stromer describes Spinosaurus from Bahariya Oasis, Egypt: a long-snouted, sail-backed predator known from fragmentary remains.

title: The Spinosaurus type is destroyed
subject: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
summary: The Munich museum holding Stromer's Egyptian collections is hit during bombing. The Spinosaurus type material is lost; only drawings, photographs and casts remain. The loss shapes every later reconstruction.

title: Deinonychus and the Dinosaur Renaissance
subject: Deinonychus antirrhopus
summary: John Ostrom's monograph describes an agile, bird-like predator with a sickle claw. Its anatomy supports active, endothermic dinosaurs and helps launch the Dinosaur Renaissance.

title: A fish-eating dinosaur from Surrey
subject: Baryonyx walkeri
summary: Charig and Milner name Baryonyx from a partial skeleton found at Smokejacks Brickworks in 1983. Fish scales and teeth in the body-cavity region provide direct evidence of fish eating.

title: Feathers on Velociraptor
subject: Velociraptor mongoliensis
summary: A Velociraptor ulna preserves regularly spaced quill knobs, direct osteological evidence for large forearm feathers. The discovery closes a gap between inferred and observed feathered dromaeosaurs.

title: An articulated stegosaur
subject: Stegosaurus stenops
summary: Maidment and colleagues describe NHMUK PV R36730, an exceptionally complete Stegosaurus from Wyoming that preserves much of the skeleton and armour in articulation.

title: A semiaquatic Spinosaurus
subject: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
summary: Ibrahim and colleagues describe a partial skeleton from Morocco and propose it as a neotype, a designation later disputed by Evers and colleagues. Short hind limbs, dense bones and a long snout lead them to propose a semiaquatic, possibly quadrupedal animal.

title: A paddle tail
subject: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
summary: The tail of the Moroccan specimen is described, with tall distal neural spines and elongated chevrons forming a paddle. The authors argue for tail-propelled swimming.

title: The aquatic hypothesis is challenged
subject: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
summary: Studies argue for and against habitual aquatic behaviour. Hone and Holtz propose a shoreline generalist; Sereno and colleagues reconstruct a more terrestrial, bipedal animal; a 2024 paper questions the bone-density methods behind the aquatic inference.
